question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

"The scientist discovered a new planet."
option_1: A new planet was discovered by the scientist.
option_2: A new planet is discovered by the scientist.
option_3: A new planet had discovered by the scientist.
option_4: A new planet was being discovered.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. A new planet was discovered by the scientist.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The given sentence is in the Simple Past Tense (Active Voice): Subject + V2 + Object → 'The scientist discovered a new planet.'

 

• Passive of Simple Past = Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject.

 

• 'A new planet' (singular) becomes the subject, so 'was' is used → 'A new planet was discovered by the scientist.'

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (A new planet is discovered by the scientist): 'is discovered' is Simple Present passive — the tense has been wrongly changed from past to present.

 

• Option 3 (A new planet had discovered by the scientist): 'had discovered' is an active Past Perfect form; passive needs 'be + V3', and 'had discovered by' is ungrammatical.

 

• Option 4 (A new planet was being discovered): 'was being discovered' is Past Continuous passive, and the agent 'by the scientist' has also been dropped.

 

• Passive formula chart: Simple Present – is/am/are + V3; Simple Past – was/were + V3; Present Continuous – is/am/are being + V3; Past Continuous – was/were being + V3; Perfect tenses – has/have/had been + V3; Future – will be + V3.

 

NOTE

 

• In voice change, the tense of the sentence never changes; only the subject and object interchange and the verb takes the form 'be + V3'.

question: Choose the correctly spelt word:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Successful.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct spelling is Successful (सफल) — meaning achieving the desired aim.

 

• Remember the pattern: su-cc-e-ss-ful → double 'c', double 's' and a single 'l'.

 

• The suffix '-ful' always has one 'l' when attached to a word (success + ful = successful).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (Succesful): 'Succesful' – one 's' is missing in the middle (succe-s-ful).

 

• Option 2 (Successfull): 'Successfull' – the suffix '-ful' never takes double 'l'.

 

• Option 4 (Succesfull): 'Succesfull' – has two mistakes: missing 's' and an extra 'l'.

 

• Similar '-ful' words: beautiful, careful, grateful, wonderful, faithful, plentiful — all with a single 'l'.

 

• Derived forms: success (noun), succeed (verb), successfully (adverb – here the 'l' doubles because '-ly' is added).

 

NOTE

 

• 'Full' (with double l) is a separate word; as a suffix it always becomes '-ful'.

question: Choose the correctly spelt word:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Idiosyncrasy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct spelling is Idiosyncrasy (व्यक्तिगत विशेषता / सनक) — a peculiar habit or way of behaving that is typical of a particular person.

 

• It comes from Greek idios (own, personal) + syn (together) + krasis (mixture).

 

• Spelling tips: begins with 'Idio-' (like idiom, idiot) and ends with '-crasy' (NOT '-cracy' like democracy).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (Ideosyncrasy): 'Ideosyncrasy' – wrong prefix; it is 'idio-', not 'ideo-'.

 

• Option 3 (Idiosynchrasy): 'Idiosynchrasy' – there is no 'h' after 'c'; 'synch-' is wrongly borrowed from 'synchronise'.

 

• Option 4 (Idiosyncresy): 'Idiosyncresy' – the ending is '-crasy', not '-cresy'.

 

• Adjective form: idiosyncratic. Example: His idiosyncratic style of dressing made him stand out.

 

• Synonyms: quirk, peculiarity, eccentricity, oddity, mannerism.

 

NOTE

 

• Frequently misspelt SSC words ending in '-crasy'/'-cracy': idiosyncrasy (-crasy) vs democracy, bureaucracy, autocracy (-cracy).

question:
In the following question, a sentence has been given in Indirect Speech. Choose the correct Direct Speech form.

She said that only if he had studied regularly would he have passed the exam.
option_1: She said, “Only if he studied regularly he would have passed the exam.”
option_2: She said, “Only if he had studied regularly he would pass the exam.”
option_3: She said, “Only if he had studied regularly would he have passed the exam.”
option_4: She said, “Only he would pass the exam if he had studied regularly.”
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. She said, “Only if he had studied regularly would he have passed the exam.”

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The indirect sentence contains an inverted third conditional: 'only if he had studied regularly would he have passed the exam.'

 

• This is an unreal past condition (Type 3: If + had + V3, would have + V3). Such conditional sentences do not change their tense in reported speech, so the direct speech keeps exactly the same form.

 

• When a sentence begins with 'Only if', the main clause takes inversion (auxiliary before subject): 'would he have passed'.

 

• Hence: She said, “Only if he had studied regularly would he have passed the exam.”

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: 'Only if he studied regularly he would have passed' – mixes a Type 2 if-clause with a Type 3 main clause, and there is no inversion after 'Only if'.

 

• Option 2: 'he would pass' – wrong conditional (Type 2 result) and inversion is missing.

 

• Option 4: 'Only he would pass the exam…' – the word order changes the meaning ('only he' = nobody else) and the tense pattern is wrong.

 

• Inversion after restrictive expressions: Only if…, Only when…, Only after…, Not only…, Never…, Hardly…, Seldom… → auxiliary + subject. Example: Only when he apologised did she forgive him.

 

• Type 3 conditional: If + had + V3 → would/could/might have + V3 (an imaginary situation in the past).

 

NOTE

 

• In narration, past perfect and unreal conditional (would have + V3) forms remain unchanged when converted either way.

question:
Choose the word which is most nearly the same in meaning to the underlined word.

The students who graduated from that school are adept at playing musical instruments
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. proficient.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Adept (adjective) means very skilled or proficient at something (कुशल / निपुण).

 

• Proficient means competent or skilled in doing something — an exact synonym.

 

• The sentence says the students are highly skilled at playing musical instruments; 'proficient' fits perfectly.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (comfortable): 'Comfortable' means at ease; being comfortable does not mean being skilled.

 

• Option 3 (careful): 'Careful' means cautious; it has no connection with skill.

 

• Option 4 (proverbial): 'Proverbial' means referred to in a proverb or well known; unrelated to skill.

 

• Synonyms of adept: skilful, expert, accomplished, masterly, dexterous, deft. Antonyms: inept, clumsy, unskilled, amateurish.

 

• Usage: adept at/in something – She is adept at solving puzzles.

 

NOTE

 

• Do not confuse adept (skilled) with adapt (to adjust) and adopt (to take up/accept) — a favourite SSC confusable set.

question:
Choose the word which is most nearly the same in meaning to the underlined word.

Racial segregation was a reality in many countries.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. separation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Segregation (noun) means the action of setting someone or something apart from others; separation, especially on the basis of race (पृथक्करण / अलगाव).

 

• 'Racial segregation' = keeping people of different races apart in schools, transport, housing, etc.

 

• Hence, separation is the closest in meaning.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (integration): 'Integration' means bringing together into one whole — it is the antonym of segregation.

 

• Option 2 (education): 'Education' means the process of teaching and learning; unrelated.

 

• Option 4 (desertion): 'Desertion' means abandoning a person, place or duty; it is not about separating groups.

 

• Synonyms: separation, isolation, partition, apartheid, discrimination. Antonyms: integration, unification, desegregation, inclusion.

 

• Historical note: 'Apartheid' was the system of racial segregation in South Africa (1948–1994).

 

NOTE

 

• Verb: segregate; adjective: segregated. Example: The waste should be segregated into dry and wet categories.

question: What is the synonym of "Apathy"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Indifference.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Apathy (noun) means lack of interest, enthusiasm or concern (उदासीनता).

 

• Indifference means lack of interest or concern — an exact synonym.

 

• Word origin: Greek 'a-' (without) + 'pathos' (feeling) → without feeling.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (Interest): 'Interest' is the opposite of apathy.

 

• Option 2 (Concern): 'Concern' means care or worry about something — an antonym.

 

• Option 4 (Compassion): 'Compassion' means sympathy and concern for others' suffering — opposite in sense.

 

• Synonyms: indifference, unconcern, passivity, lethargy, listlessness. Antonyms: enthusiasm, interest, zeal, passion, concern.

 

• Adjective: apathetic – The voters were apathetic about the election.

 

NOTE

 

• Related 'pathos' words: sympathy (feeling with), empathy (feeling into), antipathy (feeling against), apathy (no feeling).

question:
Choose the one word substitute for the below sentence.

Priyanka enjoyed studying texts filled with expressions that were commonly used in ancient times but have since fallen out of general use.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Archaic.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Archaic (adjective) means very old or old-fashioned; (of a word or style) no longer in everyday use but kept for special purposes (पुरातन / अप्रचलित).

 

• The sentence describes expressions 'commonly used in ancient times but have since fallen out of general use' — this is exactly the meaning of 'archaic'.

 

• Examples of archaic words: thee, thou, thy, hath, doth, forsooth.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (Technical): 'Technical' relates to a particular subject, art or craft; not about old usage.

 

• Option 3 (Modern Slang): 'Modern Slang' refers to informal, recent expressions — the opposite of ancient usage.

 

• Option 4 (Trending): 'Trending' means currently popular — again the opposite idea.

 

• Synonyms: obsolete, antiquated, outdated, outmoded. Antonyms: modern, contemporary, current, up-to-date.

 

• Obsolete = no longer used at all; Archaic = old but still occasionally used for effect.

 

NOTE

 

• Related one-word substitutions: Anachronism – something out of its proper time; Neologism – a newly coined word.

question:
Choose the one word substitute for the below sentence.

Rahul impressed everyone with his ability to create detailed plans for new and innovative buildings.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Architect.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An Architect is a person who designs buildings and prepares detailed plans for their construction (वास्तुकार).

 

• The sentence mentions the 'ability to create detailed plans for new and innovative buildings' — the precise work of an architect.

 

• Origin: Greek 'arkhi-' (chief) + 'tekton' (builder).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (Mason): A 'Mason' builds with stone or bricks; he constructs, he does not design.

 

• Option 3 (Carpenter): A 'Carpenter' makes and repairs wooden objects and structures.

 

• Option 4 (Surveyor): A 'Surveyor' measures and examines land or property; he does not design buildings.

 

• Related one-words: Civil engineer – designs and supervises construction of roads, bridges, etc.; Draughtsman – prepares technical drawings; Interior designer – plans inside spaces.

 

• Architecture = the art and science of designing buildings.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Architect' is also used figuratively: the architect of the plan = the person who conceived it.

question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

Fewer of the experimental designs (1)/ was compatible with the theoretical model (2)/ proposed by the research team (3)/ in their meta-analysis. (4)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (2).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The subject of the sentence is 'Fewer of the experimental designs', which refers to a plural noun (designs).

 

• A plural subject takes a plural verb; hence 'was compatible' must be 'were compatible'.

 

• Correct sentence: Fewer of the experimental designs were compatible with the theoretical model proposed by the research team in their meta-analysis.

 

• The error lies in part (2).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: 'Fewer of the experimental designs' is correct — 'fewer' is rightly used with a countable plural noun.

 

• Option 3: 'proposed by the research team' is a correct past-participle phrase qualifying 'model'.

 

• Option 4: 'in their meta-analysis' is correct; 'team' acting as individuals takes 'their'.

 

• Rule: With 'fewer of / many of / a few of / several of / both of + plural noun', the verb is plural.

 

• 'Fewer' is used with countable nouns (fewer books); 'less' with uncountable nouns (less water).

 

NOTE

 

• Always locate the true subject; do not be misled by the words between the subject and the verb.

question:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.

We don't have to go to the party, don’t we? We can stay at home.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. don't we.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The sentence contains a question tag error. Rule: a negative statement takes a positive tag and a positive statement takes a negative tag.

 

• 'We don't have to go to the party' is a negative statement, so the tag must be positive: 'do we?'

 

• Correct sentence: We don't have to go to the party, do we? We can stay at home.

 

• Hence, the error is in 'don't we'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (have to go): 'have to go' is correct — 'have to' expresses necessity and 'don't have to' means it is not necessary.

 

• Option 3 (can stay): 'can stay' is correct — modal 'can' + base form 'stay'.

 

• Option 4 (to the party): 'to the party' is correct — 'go to' a place/event.

 

• With 'have to' (main verb 'have'), the tag uses the auxiliary do/does/did: You have to leave, don't you? / She doesn't have to come, does she?

 

• Other tag rules: I am → aren't I?; Let's → shall we?; Imperative → will you?; Nobody/Nothing/Hardly/Seldom → positive tag.

 

NOTE

 

• The tag always repeats the auxiliary of the statement with the opposite polarity and uses a pronoun for the subject.

question:
The sentence below has errors in two parts which are highlighted in bold. Identify the same.

The reef is on risk of (A) losing its coveted World Heritage Status on occasion of (B) ocean warming, fuelled by(C) climate change, which is damaging its health(D).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. BA.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Part (A): 'is on risk of' is incorrect. The correct phrase is 'at risk of' (in danger of) — The reef is at risk of losing its status.

 

• Part (B): 'on occasion of' is incorrect in this sense; 'on the occasion of' means at the time of a celebration. To express cause, we use 'on account of' / 'because of' / 'due to'.

 

• Correct sentence: The reef is at risk of losing its coveted World Heritage Status on account of ocean warming, fuelled by climate change, which is damaging its health.

 

• Parts (C) 'fuelled by' and (D) 'damaging its health' are correct. So the erroneous parts are B and A.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (CD): 'CD' – 'fuelled by' (driven by) and 'damaging its health' are both grammatically correct.

 

• Option 3 (AC): 'AC' – A is wrong, but C ('fuelled by climate change') is correct.

 

• Option 4 (CB): 'CB' – B is wrong, but C is correct.

 

• Fixed phrases: at risk of, at stake, at the mercy of, on account of, on behalf of, in spite of, in view of, by virtue of.

 

• 'On occasion' (without 'the') = occasionally, sometimes.

 

NOTE

 

• The option 'BA' simply lists the two wrong parts; the order of letters does not matter for the answer.

question: What is the meaning of the phrase "Elephantine task"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. A huge difficult task.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Elephantine task means a task that is enormous, heavy and very difficult to accomplish (भारी/विशाल कठिन कार्य).

 

• 'Elephantine' (adjective) = resembling an elephant in size; huge, massive, clumsy.

 

• Hence, 'A huge difficult task' is the correct meaning.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (A secret mission): 'A secret mission' – nothing in 'elephantine' suggests secrecy.

 

• Option 3 (A simple chore): 'A simple chore' – the opposite of an elephantine (huge) task.

 

• Option 4 (A task involving elephants): 'A task involving elephants' – a literal but wrong interpretation; the phrase is figurative.

 

• Similar expressions: Herculean task (needing great strength/effort), uphill task (difficult to do), tall order (a difficult demand).

 

• Synonyms of elephantine: gigantic, colossal, mammoth, immense, gargantuan.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Herculean task' is the most frequently asked equivalent of 'elephantine task' in SSC exams.

question: What does the phrase "Pass the buck" mean?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. To evade responsibility.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pass the buck means to shift responsibility or blame for something onto someone else; to evade responsibility (ज़िम्मेदारी दूसरे पर डालना).

 

• Origin: In poker, a marker called the 'buck' was passed to the next player to show whose turn it was to deal.

 

• Example: When the project failed, the manager tried to pass the buck to his juniors.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (To bet money): 'To bet money' – although linked to poker, the idiom is not about betting.

 

• Option 3 (To speak briefly): 'To speak briefly' – unrelated.

 

• Option 4 (To transfer something): 'To transfer something' – too literal; the idiom specifically means shifting responsibility/blame.

 

• Related: 'The buck stops here' – I accept full responsibility (made famous by US President Harry Truman).

 

• Similar idioms: pass the baton (hand over a duty), wash one's hands of (refuse responsibility).

 

NOTE

 

• 'Buck' in informal American English also means a dollar — but that meaning is not used in this idiom.

question:
Identify the error in the below-given sentence.

"The police has arrested the suspect in the case".
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. has.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Police' is a collective noun that is always plural in form and usage; it always takes a plural verb.

 

• Therefore, 'The police has arrested' should be 'The police have arrested the suspect in the case'.

 

• The error lies in 'has'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (police): 'police' is the correct noun; the error is in the verb that agrees with it.

 

• Option 2 (suspect): 'suspect' is correct as a noun meaning a person thought to be guilty.

 

• Option 3 (arrested): 'arrested' is the correct past participle in the present perfect tense.

 

• Other nouns always used as plural: cattle, people, gentry, clergy, peasantry, vermin, poultry (The cattle are grazing).

 

• Nouns that look plural but take singular verbs: news, mathematics, physics, innings, measles, politics (as a subject).

 

NOTE

 

• To refer to one member, say 'a policeman / a police officer', never 'a police'.

question:
Find the homonym error.

Sentence: She will insure that everyone is invited.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. insure.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Insure means to arrange financial protection against loss (बीमा करना) — e.g., insure a car/house.

 

• Ensure means to make certain that something happens (सुनिश्चित करना).

 

• The sentence means she will make certain that everyone is invited, so the correct word is 'ensure': She will ensure that everyone is invited.

 

• Hence, the homonym error is in 'insure'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (everyone): 'everyone' is correct – an indefinite pronoun taking the singular verb 'is'.

 

• Option 3 (is): 'is' is correct – agrees with the singular 'everyone'.

 

• Option 4 (invited): 'invited' is correct – past participle in the passive 'is invited'.

 

• The trio: Ensure (make certain), Insure (protect financially), Assure (remove someone's doubts/promise). Example: I assure you that I will ensure the house is insured.

 

NOTE

 

• Confusable pairs often asked: affect/effect, accept/except, principal/principle, stationary/stationery, complement/compliment.

question:
Choose the word that best completes the sentence.

The climbers reached the ______ of the mountain by dawn.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. peak.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Peak (noun) means the pointed top of a mountain; summit (चोटी / शिखर).

 

• The climbers reached the peak (top) of the mountain by dawn.

 

• 'Peek', 'peak' and 'pique' are homophones – same sound, different spelling and meaning.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (peek): 'Peek' means to look quickly or secretly (e.g., peek through the curtain).

 

• Option 3 (pique): 'Pique' means a feeling of irritation or to arouse curiosity (e.g., pique one's interest).

 

• Option 4 (pick): 'Pick' means to choose or to pluck; it does not refer to the top of a mountain.

 

• Other meanings of peak: the highest point of activity – peak hours, at the peak of her career.

 

• Synonyms of peak (mountain): summit, pinnacle, apex, crest, zenith.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Pique one's curiosity' (NOT 'peak') is a common error in SSC spotting questions.

question:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'

The car was parked right out the gate, blocking the driveway.
option_3: in the front of the gate
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. in front of the gate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The underlined phrase 'out the gate' is incorrect and incomplete in standard English.

 

• The correct compound preposition is 'in front of' (सामने), which shows position before something.

 

• Correct sentence: The car was parked right in front of the gate, blocking the driveway.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (in front to the gate): 'in front to the gate' – 'in front' is always followed by 'of', never 'to'.

 

• Option 3 (in the front of the gate): 'in the front of the gate' – 'in the front of' means inside the front part of something (e.g., in the front of the bus); here the car is outside, facing the gate.

 

• Option 4 (No substitution): 'No substitution' – 'out the gate' is ungrammatical/informal, so a substitution is required.

 

• In front of = outside, facing something (a tree in front of the house). In the front of = inside, in the forward part (the driver sits in the front of the car).

 

• Other compound prepositions: on top of, in spite of, by means of, instead of, on behalf of.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Out of' is used for movement from inside to outside: He walked out of the gate.

question:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'

The general was entrusted for the safety of the troops.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. entrusted with.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The verb 'entrust' is used with the prepositions 'with' and 'to' in two patterns:

 

• Entrust somebody WITH something → The general was entrusted with the safety of the troops (the person is the subject in passive).

 

• Entrust something TO somebody → The safety of the troops was entrusted to the general.

 

• Since 'the general' (person) is the subject here, 'entrusted with' is correct.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (entrusted by): 'entrusted by' – 'by' would introduce the doer who entrusted, not the responsibility given.

 

• Option 3 (entrusted to): 'entrusted to' – would be correct only if the thing entrusted were the subject (The safety … was entrusted to the general).

 

• Option 4 (No substitution): 'No substitution' – 'entrusted for' is incorrect usage.

 

• Entrust (सौंपना) = to give someone responsibility for a task or thing. Synonyms: charge with, consign, delegate, assign.

 

• Similar pattern verbs: present somebody with something / present something to somebody; provide somebody with something / provide something for somebody.

 

NOTE

 

• Remember: PERSON + entrusted + WITH + THING; THING + entrusted + TO + PERSON.

question:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'

The company is currently under threat from a potential lawsuit.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. under threat of.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiomatic expression is 'under threat of' + the harm/danger that may happen (e.g., under threat of closure, under threat of lawsuit, under threat of death).

 

• A 'potential lawsuit' is the action that is threatened, so 'under threat of a potential lawsuit' is correct.

 

• 'Under threat from' is used with the source/agent of the danger (e.g., under threat from terrorists, under threat from rising sea levels).

 

• Correct sentence: The company is currently under threat of a potential lawsuit.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (under threat by): 'under threat by' – 'by' is not used with 'threat' in this expression.

 

• Option 3 (on threat from): 'on threat from' – 'on threat' is not an acceptable English phrase; the phrase is 'under threat'.

 

• Option 4 (No substitution): 'No substitution' – 'from' wrongly treats the lawsuit as the source rather than the threatened action.

 

• Other 'under' phrases: under pressure, under consideration, under arrest, under construction, under control, under oath.

 

• The phrase 'under threat' means at risk of being harmed or lost.

 

NOTE

 

• Tip: of + WHAT may happen (under threat of eviction); from + WHO/WHAT causes it (under threat from the landlord).

question:
Change the following active voice sentence into passive voice by selecting the correct option.

The Indian Space Research Organisation will launch the Gaganyaan mission next year.
option_1: Gaganyaan mission is being launched by ISRO next year.
option_2: Gaganyaan mission will be launched by ISRO next year.
option_3: The Gaganyaan mission has been launched by ISRO next year.
option_4: The Gaganyaan mission is launched by ISRO next year.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Gaganyaan mission will be launched by ISRO next year.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The given sentence is in the Simple Future Tense: Subject + will + V1 + Object.

 

• Passive of Simple Future = Object + will be + V3 + by + Agent.

 

• Hence: Gaganyaan mission will be launched by ISRO next year. (ISRO is the abbreviation of the Indian Space Research Organisation.)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: 'is being launched' is Present Continuous passive — the tense is changed.

 

• Option 3: 'has been launched … next year' is Present Perfect passive; it is also illogical with the future time marker 'next year'.

 

• Option 4: 'is launched' is Simple Present passive — the tense is changed.

 

• Future tense passive forms: will be + V3 (Simple Future); will have been + V3 (Future Perfect). Future Continuous and Future Perfect Continuous are normally not changed into passive.

 

• Gaganyaan is India's first human spaceflight programme undertaken by ISRO (headquarters: Bengaluru).

 

NOTE

 

• Time expressions (next year, yesterday, tomorrow) remain unchanged in voice change and help confirm the tense.

question:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'

The travellers met off an accident on the way.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. met with.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct phrasal verb is 'meet with', which means to experience something unpleasant or unexpected, such as an accident (दुर्घटना का शिकार होना).

 

• Correct sentence: The travellers met with an accident on the way.

 

• 'Meet with an accident' is a fixed collocation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (met of): 'met of' – 'meet' is never followed by 'of'.

 

• Option 2 (met): 'met' alone means encountered a person (I met my friend); one does not simply 'meet an accident'.

 

• Option 4 (No substitution): 'No substitution' – 'met off' is incorrect; 'off' does not collocate with 'meet' in this sense.

 

• Other uses of 'meet with': meet with success/failure/approval/opposition/resistance; meet with someone (have a meeting, American usage).

 

• Similar collocations: have an accident, suffer a loss, face a problem.

 

NOTE

 

• SSC often tests 'met with an accident' in error-spotting — omitting 'with' is marked as an error.

question:
Change the following passive voice sentence into active voice by selecting the correct option.

The Railways Ministry has been upgrading railway stations across India over the last decade.
option_1: Railway stations across India have been being upgraded by the Railways Ministry over the last decade.
option_2: Railway stations have been upgraded by the Railways Ministry over the last decade.
option_3: Railway stations across India have been upgraded by the Railways Ministry over the last decade.
option_4: Railway stations across India are being upgraded by the Railways Ministry over the last decade.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Railway stations across India have been being upgraded by the Railways Ministry over the last decade.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The given sentence is in the Present Perfect Continuous Tense (active): Subject + has/have been + V-ing + Object → 'The Railways Ministry has been upgrading railway stations…'

 

• The exact passive structure of this tense is Object + has/have been being + V3 + by + Agent.

 

• Object 'railway stations across India' is plural → 'have been being upgraded': Railway stations across India have been being upgraded by the Railways Ministry over the last decade.

 

• This keeps the tense (continuing action), the complete object ('across India') and the time phrase unchanged, so Option 1 is the grammatically faithful passive. This paper itself accepts the same pattern in Q.125 and Q.126 ('has been being audited', 'has been being constructed').

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: 'Railway stations have been upgraded' – changes the tense to Present Perfect and also drops 'across India'.

 

• Option 3: 'have been upgraded' – changes the tense from Present Perfect Continuous (ongoing) to Present Perfect (completed), which alters the meaning of an action still in progress. (The provisional key marks this option, treating 'have been being' as awkward; on strict voice-change rules, Option 1 is the exact passive.)

 

• Option 4: 'are being upgraded' – Present Continuous passive; the tense is changed and it does not fit 'over the last decade'.

 

• Traditional grammar books say Perfect Continuous tenses are 'rarely' used in the passive because 'been being' sounds heavy; however, when an option with the exact form is given, it is the correct transformation.

 

• Passive of Present Perfect Continuous: has/have been being + V3; Past Perfect Continuous: had been being + V3.

 

NOTE

 

• The instruction in the question says 'passive into active', but the given sentence is actually active and all options are passive — so the task is Active → Passive.

question: Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'The doctor has advised me to cut down in my sugar intake to stay healthy.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Cut down on.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct phrasal verb is 'cut down on', meaning to reduce the amount of something one uses or consumes (कम करना).

 

• Correct sentence: The doctor has advised me to cut down on my sugar intake to stay healthy.

 

• 'Cut down' alone means to fell (a tree) or reduce; when followed by the thing reduced, it takes 'on'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (Cut off on): 'Cut off on' – 'cut off' means to disconnect or isolate; 'cut off on' is not a valid phrase.

 

• Option 2 (Cut down for): 'Cut down for' – 'for' does not collocate with 'cut down' in this sense.

 

• Option 4 (No substitution): 'No substitution' – 'cut down in' is incorrect.

 

• Other 'cut' phrasal verbs: cut in (interrupt), cut off (disconnect), cut out (stop doing/eating something), cut back on (reduce spending), cut across (take a shorter route).

 

• Synonyms of cut down on: reduce, curtail, lessen, decrease.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Cut back on' is a close equivalent of 'cut down on' and is also correct in formal contexts.

question:
Change the following passive voice sentence into active voice by selecting the correct option.

Public expenditure has been being audited closely by the Finance Ministry for the past six months.
option_1: Public expenditure has been audited closely by the Finance Ministry for the past six months.
option_2: The Finance Ministry has been auditing public expenditure closely for the past six months.
option_3: Public expenditure is being audited closely by the Finance Ministry for the past six months.
option_4: The Finance Ministry is auditing public expenditure closely for the past six months.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The Finance Ministry has been auditing public expenditure closely for the past six months.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The given sentence is in the passive form of the Present Perfect Continuous Tense: 'Public expenditure has been being audited … by the Finance Ministry'.

 

• To convert into active voice, the agent 'the Finance Ministry' becomes the subject and the verb becomes has been + V-ing.

 

• Active: The Finance Ministry has been auditing public expenditure closely for the past six months.

 

• The time phrase 'for the past six months' also confirms the Present Perfect Continuous tense.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: This is still in passive voice and the tense is changed to Present Perfect.

 

• Option 3: This is also passive, in Present Continuous tense.

 

• Option 4: 'is auditing' is Present Continuous active — the tense is changed and it does not suit 'for the past six months'.

 

• Active Present Perfect Continuous: has/have been + V-ing; Passive: has/have been being + V3.

 

• 'For' + period of time (for six months), 'since' + point of time (since January) are typical markers of perfect continuous tenses.

 

NOTE

 

• In voice change, check three things: correct subject–object swap, same tense, and unchanged adverbs/time expressions.

question:
Change the following active voice sentence into passive voice by selecting the correct option.

They have been constructing the new metro line in Pune for two years.
option_1: The new metro line in Pune is constructed for two years.
option_2: The new metro line in Pune has been constructed for two years.
option_3: The new metro line in Pune has been being constructed for two years.
option_4: The new metro line in Pune will be constructed for two years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The new metro line in Pune has been being constructed for two years.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The given sentence is in the Present Perfect Continuous Tense (active): 'They have been constructing the new metro line…'

 

• Passive = Object + has/have been being + V3. The object 'the new metro line' is singular → 'has been being constructed'.

 

• 'They' is an indefinite agent, so 'by them' is omitted.

 

• Passive: The new metro line in Pune has been being constructed for two years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: 'is constructed' – Simple Present passive; tense changed.

 

• Option 2: 'has been constructed' – Present Perfect passive; it shows a completed action, whereas the original shows a continuing action.

 

• Option 4: 'will be constructed' – Simple Future passive; tense changed.

 

• When the subject of the active sentence is indefinite (they, people, someone, somebody, one), the agent is usually dropped in the passive.

 

• Pune Metro is operated by Maha-Metro (Maharashtra Metro Rail Corporation Limited).

 

NOTE

 

• Continuous passive always uses 'being': is being + V3, was being + V3, has been being + V3.

question:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.

The report must have been completed by the team before the deadline.
option_1: The team must have completed the report before the deadline.
option_2: The team must complete the report before the deadline.
option_3: The team should complete the report before the deadline.
option_4: The team must had completed the report before the deadline.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. The team must have completed the report before the deadline.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The given sentence is a passive with a modal perfect: must + have been + V3 → 'The report must have been completed by the team'.

 

• Active form of modal perfect = Subject + must have + V3 + Object.

 

• Active: The team must have completed the report before the deadline. ('must have' expresses a logical conclusion about the past.)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: 'must complete' – modal present form; it changes the time reference from past to present/future.

 

• Option 3: 'should complete' – changes the modal (must → should) and the time.

 

• Option 4: 'must had completed' – grammatically wrong; a modal is always followed by the base form ('have'), never 'had'.

 

• Modal passive formulas: modal + be + V3 (present/future); modal + have been + V3 (past). Example: can be done / could have been done.

 

• 'Must have + V3' = strong deduction about the past; 'should have + V3' = unfulfilled duty in the past.

 

NOTE

 

• The modal itself never changes during voice conversion.

question:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.

The injured man was given first aid by the volunteers.
option_1: The volunteers gave the injured man first aid.
option_2: The volunteers were given first aid by the injured man.
option_3: The injured man gave the volunteers first aid.
option_4: The injured man was giving first aid to the volunteers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. The volunteers gave the injured man first aid.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The given sentence is in the Simple Past passive with the indirect object as subject: 'The injured man was given first aid by the volunteers.'

 

• 'Give' takes two objects — indirect (the injured man) and direct (first aid).

 

• Active: The volunteers gave the injured man first aid. (Agent 'the volunteers' becomes the subject; verb in V2.)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Reverses the roles — says the volunteers received first aid, and it is still passive.

 

• Option 3: Reverses the doer and receiver: the injured man is shown giving first aid.

 

• Option 4: Wrong doer and wrong tense (Past Continuous active).

 

• Verbs with two objects (give, tell, send, show, offer, teach, lend) can form two passives: The injured man was given first aid / First aid was given to the injured man.

 

• First aid (प्राथमिक चिकित्सा) = immediate help given to an injured person before full medical treatment.

 

NOTE

 

• In active-passive questions, first identify the DOER — the doer in the 'by' phrase becomes the subject in the active voice.

question:
Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:

Rony will say to the stranger, “My father is playing volleyball with his friends in the field presently.”
option_1: Rony will say to the stranger that his father was playing volleyball with his friends in the field presently.
option_2: Rony will say to the stranger that his father was playing volleyball with his friends in the field lately.
option_3: Rony said to the stranger that his father was playing volleyball with his friends in the field presently.
option_4: Rony will say to the stranger that his father is playing volleyball with his friends in the field presently.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Rony will say to the stranger that his father is playing volleyball with his friends in the field presently.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The reporting verb 'will say' is in the future tense. Rule: if the reporting verb is in the present or future tense, the tense of the reported speech does not change.

 

• So 'is playing' remains 'is playing'; 'My father' changes to 'his father' (first person → according to the subject Rony).

 

• Words like 'presently' remain unchanged because the time frame is not shifted.

 

• Indirect: Rony will say to the stranger that his father is playing volleyball with his friends in the field presently.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Changes 'is playing' to 'was playing' though the reporting verb is future.

 

• Option 2: Changes the tense and also wrongly changes 'presently' to 'lately', altering the meaning.

 

• Option 3: Changes the reporting verb itself ('will say' → 'said'), which is never done.

 

• Present/future reporting verbs (says, is saying, has said, will say) → no change of tense in the reported clause.

 

• Past reporting verb (said) → backshift: is → was, am → was, has → had, will → would.

 

NOTE

 

• The reporting verb is never changed in tense during narration conversion; only the reported clause may change.

question:
Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:

Ruby said, "I was driving when you called me yesterday."
option_1: Ruby said that she had been driving when he had called her the day before.
option_2: Ruby said that she was driving when he had called her the day before.
option_3: Ruby said that she had been driving when he called her the day after.
option_4: Ruby said that she was driving when he called her the day before.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Ruby said that she had been driving when he had called her the day before.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The reporting verb 'said' is in the past tense, so the reported speech undergoes backshift.

 

• Past Continuous 'was driving' → Past Perfect Continuous 'had been driving'; Simple Past 'called' → Past Perfect 'had called'.

 

• Pronouns: I → she, you → he (the listener), me → her; time: yesterday → the day before / the previous day.

 

• Indirect: Ruby said that she had been driving when he had called her the day before.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Keeps 'was driving' unchanged; according to the backshift rule it should become 'had been driving'.

 

• Option 3: 'the day after' is wrong; 'yesterday' becomes 'the day before' (the day after = tomorrow's change).

 

• Option 4: Does not backshift either verb.

 

• Backshift chart: V1 → V2; V2 → had + V3; is/am/are + V-ing → was/were + V-ing; was/were + V-ing → had been + V-ing; will → would; can → could.

 

• Time changes: now → then; today → that day; tomorrow → the next day; yesterday → the day before; ago → before.

 

NOTE

 

• In modern usage the past tense in time clauses is sometimes kept unchanged, but in SSC exams the complete backshift rule is followed.

question:
Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:

The Brahmin said to the beggar, "Why don't you work in a sweatshop and earn a few bucks and manage your family rather than begging?"
option_1: The Brahmin asked the beggar why he had not worked in a sweatshop and earned a few bucks and manage his family rather than begging.
option_2: The Brahmin asked the beggar why he not worked in a sweatshop and earned a few bucks and manage his family rather than begging.
option_3: The Brahmin asked the beggar why he didn't work in a sweatshop and earn a few bucks and manage his family rather than begging.
option_4: The Brahmin asked the beggar why he is not working in a sweatshop earning a few bucks and managing his family rather than begging.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The Brahmin asked the beggar why he didn't work in a sweatshop and earn a few bucks and manage his family rather than begging.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The direct speech is an interrogative sentence beginning with a wh-word ('Why'), so 'said to' changes to 'asked' and the wh-word itself acts as the connector.

 

• The question is changed into an assertive (statement) order: subject + verb, and the question mark is removed.

 

• Simple Present 'don't you work … earn … manage' backshifts to Simple Past: 'he didn't work … and earn … and manage'; 'you/your' → he/his.

 

• Indirect: The Brahmin asked the beggar why he didn't work in a sweatshop and earn a few bucks and manage his family rather than begging.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: 'had not worked … and earned … and manage' – wrong backshift (Present → Past Perfect) and the parallel verbs are not consistent.

 

• Option 2: 'why he not worked' – omits the auxiliary 'did'; ungrammatical.

 

• Option 4: 'why he is not working' – no backshift after the past reporting verb, and the verbs are changed into -ing forms.

 

• For wh-questions: reporting verb → asked/enquired/wanted to know; connector = the same wh-word; sentence in assertive form.

 

• For yes/no questions: connector = if/whether (He asked me if I was ready).

 

NOTE

 

• After 'did/didn't', the main verbs remain in base form, and all parallel verbs (work, earn, manage) share it.

question:
Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:

The examiner's said, "No examinee is allowed to bring any electronic gadgets into the examination hall."
option_1: The examiner's instructed that no examinee was allowed to take any electronic gadgets into the examination hall.
option_2: The examiner's instructed that no examinee were allowed to take any electronic gadgets into the examination hall.
option_3: The examiner's instructed that any examinee was allowed to brought any electronic gadgets into the examination hall.
option_4: The examiner's instructed that none of the examinee allowed to take any electronic gadgets into the examination hall.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. The examiner's instructed that no examinee was allowed to take any electronic gadgets into the examination hall.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The direct speech gives an instruction/rule, so 'said' can be changed to 'instructed'.

 

• Backshift: 'is allowed' → 'was allowed'; 'No examinee' (singular) takes the singular verb 'was'.

 

• 'bring … into' (movement towards the speaker) is changed to 'take … into' in reported speech, as the speaker's position is no longer the reference point.

 

• Indirect: The examiner's instructed that no examinee was allowed to take any electronic gadgets into the examination hall.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: 'no examinee were allowed' – subject–verb agreement error; 'no examinee' is singular.

 

• Option 3: 'any examinee was allowed to brought' – reverses the meaning (permission instead of prohibition) and 'to brought' is ungrammatical (to + V1).

 

• Option 4: 'none of the examinee allowed' – 'none of' needs a plural noun (examinees) and the verb 'was' is missing.

 

• 'No + singular noun' takes a singular verb: No student was absent. 'None of + plural noun' may take either verb in modern usage.

 

• Bring vs Take: bring = towards the speaker; take = away from the speaker.

 

NOTE

 

• The words "The examiner's" are reproduced as given in the question; the grammatically standard form would be 'The examiner'.

question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Acrimonious
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Harmonious.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Acrimonious (adjective) means (of speech or discussion) angry, bitter and full of ill feeling (कटु / तीखा).

 

• Example: an acrimonious debate / an acrimonious divorce.

 

• Its opposite is Harmonious — friendly, peaceful and free from disagreement (सामंजस्यपूर्ण).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (Bitter): 'Bitter' is a synonym of acrimonious, not an antonym.

 

• Option 3 (Angry): 'Angry' is similar in meaning to acrimonious.

 

• Option 4 (Hostile): 'Hostile' (unfriendly, antagonistic) is also a synonym.

 

• Synonyms of acrimonious: bitter, rancorous, caustic, spiteful, hostile, virulent. Antonyms: harmonious, amicable, cordial, friendly, peaceable.

 

• Noun: acrimony – bitterness or ill feeling.

 

NOTE

 

• In antonym questions, first eliminate options that are synonyms of the given word; here three options are synonyms.

question:
The following sentence has two blanks. Choose the most suitable set of prepositions from the given options to fill in the blanks and complete the sentence meaningfully:

This poem is _____ the collection ‘Gitanjali’ _____ Rabindranath Tagore.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. from, by.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• First blank: a poem is taken from a collection → 'This poem is from the collection…' (from = source/origin).

 

• Second blank: the author of a work is introduced with by → 'Gitanjali' by Rabindranath Tagore.

 

• Complete sentence: This poem is from the collection 'Gitanjali' by Rabindranath Tagore.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (of, from): 'of, from' – 'Gitanjali from Rabindranath Tagore' wrongly suggests the book was sent from him, not written by him.

 

• Option 3 (in, of): 'in, of' – 'is in the collection' is possible, but 'Gitanjali of Rabindranath Tagore' is not the standard way to state authorship.

 

• Option 4 (for, to): 'for, to' – neither preposition makes sense here.

 

• 'Gitanjali' (Song Offerings) by Rabindranath Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 — the first Nobel for an Asian.

 

• Tagore also wrote the national anthems of India (Jana Gana Mana) and Bangladesh (Amar Shonar Bangla).

 

NOTE

 

• 'By' introduces the author/creator: a novel by Premchand, a painting by Raja Ravi Varma.

question:
The following sentence has two blanks. Choose the most suitable set of prepositions from the given options to fill in the blanks and complete the sentence meaningfully.

He worked _____ the night _____ finish the project.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. through, to.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• First blank: through the night = from the beginning to the end of the night; continuously all night.

 

• Second blank: to + base verb (infinitive of purpose) = in order to → 'to finish the project'.

 

• Complete sentence: He worked through the night to finish the project.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (for, for): 'for, for' – 'worked for the night' is unidiomatic, and 'for finish' is wrong; purpose with a verb needs 'to'.

 

• Option 3 (till, without): 'till, without' – 'without finish' is ungrammatical and contradicts the sense.

 

• Option 4 (at, towards): 'at, towards' – 'at the night' is incorrect ('at night' has no article) and 'towards finish' is wrong.

 

• Infinitive of purpose: He went to the market to buy vegetables. 'For + V-ing' is used to state the function of an object (a knife for cutting).

 

• Time prepositions: at night, in the night, during the night, through/throughout the night (whole duration).

 

NOTE

 

• Never use 'for + base verb' to express purpose (✗ for finish; ✓ to finish).

question:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.

He warned the children not to play near the exposed wires as it was dangerous.
option_1: He said to the children, "Don’t play near the exposed wires as it is dangerous.”
option_2: He warned the children, "Do not play near the exposed wires as it was dangerous.”
option_3: He said to the children, "You should not play near the exposed wires as they are dangerous.”
option_4: He warned the children, "Don’t played near exposed wires as it is dangerous.”
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. He said to the children, "Don’t play near the exposed wires as it is dangerous.”

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The indirect sentence contains 'warned … not to play', which reports a negative command (imperative).

 

• In direct speech, a negative imperative begins with 'Don't / Do not' + V1; the reporting verb becomes 'said to'.

 

• The reason clause 'as it was dangerous' returns to the present tense 'as it is dangerous'.

 

• Direct: He said to the children, "Don't play near the exposed wires as it is dangerous."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Keeps 'warned' as the reporting verb for a direct quotation and retains the past tense 'was' inside the quotation.

 

• Option 3: Converts the command into advice ('You should not'), changing the sentence type, and changes 'it' to 'they'.

 

• Option 4: 'Don't played' is ungrammatical (don't + V1), and 'the' before 'exposed wires' is missing.

 

• Indirect → direct for commands: told/ordered/warned/advised + (not) to + V1 → said to, "(Don't) + V1…".

 

• In direct speech, the reported words are in the speaker's original tense (present), so backshifted forms are reversed.

 

NOTE

 

• Imperative sentences in direct speech have no subject: "Don't play…", "Please sit down."

question:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.

She exclaimed that she couldn’t believe her eyes when she saw the result.
option_1: She exclaimed, "I couldn’t believe my eyes when I saw the result!"
option_2: She said, "I can’t believe my eyes when I saw the result!"
option_3: She said, "I could not believe my eyes when I see the result!"
option_4: She exclaimed, "Could I not believe my eyes when I saw the result!"
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. She exclaimed, "I couldn’t believe my eyes when I saw the result!"

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'She exclaimed that…' shows an exclamatory sentence; in direct speech, the reporting verb 'exclaimed' can be retained and the sentence ends with an exclamation mark (!).

 

• 'she couldn't believe her eyes when she saw the result' → first person: "I couldn't believe my eyes when I saw the result!"

 

• The event (seeing the result) is already past, so 'couldn't' and 'saw' are logically retained.

 

• Direct: She exclaimed, "I couldn't believe my eyes when I saw the result!"

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: 'I can't believe … when I saw' – mixes present 'can't' with past 'saw'; tense inconsistency.

 

• Option 3: 'I could not … when I see' – mixes past 'could' with present 'see'.

 

• Option 4: 'Could I not believe…' – converts the statement into a question form; wrong word order.

 

• 'Can't believe one's eyes' (idiom) = to be very surprised by what one sees.

 

• Exclamatory narration words: exclaimed with joy/sorrow/surprise, applauded, cried out.

 

NOTE

 

• Tense consistency inside a sentence (could … saw / can … see) is a key checking point in narration options.

question:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.

The novel was written by an author who had traveled extensively.
option_1: An author who had traveled extensively wrote the novel.
option_2: The novel was written by an author who had traveled extensively.
option_3: The author wrote the novel, and he traveled extensively.
option_4: Writing the novel was done by an author who had traveled extensively.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. An author who had traveled extensively wrote the novel.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The given sentence is in the Simple Past passive: 'The novel was written by an author who had traveled extensively.'

 

• To convert to active: the agent 'an author who had traveled extensively' becomes the subject and 'was written' → 'wrote'.

 

• Active: An author who had traveled extensively wrote the novel. The relative clause stays attached to 'author'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: This is the given passive sentence repeated without any change.

 

• Option 3: Splits the sentence into two clauses, changes 'an author' to 'the author', and changes 'had traveled' to 'traveled' — the meaning and structure are altered.

 

• Option 4: Still a passive-type construction ('was done by'); it is not the active voice.

NOTE

 

• Relative clauses (who had traveled extensively) move along with the noun they describe.

question:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.

The project is rumored to be finished ahead of schedule.
option_1: Someone is rumored to finish the project ahead of schedule.
option_2: They are rumored that the project will be finished ahead of schedule.
option_3: People say that the project will be finished ahead of schedule.
option_4: They rumor that the project was finished ahead of schedule.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. People say that the project will be finished ahead of schedule.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The sentence 'The project is rumored to be finished…' is an impersonal passive with a reporting verb (say, believe, rumour, think).

 

• In such sentences the hidden agent is 'people', so the active voice is formed with 'People say that…' (or 'It is rumoured that…').

 

• 'to be finished' refers to a future event → 'will be finished'.

 

• Active: People say that the project will be finished ahead of schedule.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: 'Someone is rumored to finish the project' – still passive and it changes the meaning (someone is the subject of the rumour).

 

• Option 2: 'They are rumored that…' – ungrammatical; 'rumor' cannot be used in the passive with 'that' like this.

 

• Option 4: 'They rumor that … was finished' – changes the tense to past ('was finished') and 'rumor' is not normally used as an active reporting verb.

 

• Impersonal passive patterns: 'He is said to be rich' = People say that he is rich = It is said that he is rich.

 

• Other such verbs: believe, consider, expect, know, report, suppose, think.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Rumor' (American) = 'Rumour' (British).

question:
Choose the most suitable preposition from the given options to fill in the blank in the following sentence:

They insisted _____ paying the full amount in advance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. on.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The verb 'insist' is always followed by the preposition 'on' (insist on + noun/gerund).

 

• Correct sentence: They insisted on paying the full amount in advance.

 

• Insist on = to demand firmly (ज़िद करना / आग्रह करना).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (at): 'at' – 'insist at' is not idiomatic English.

 

• Option 3 (to): 'to' – 'insist to pay' is a common error; 'insist' does not take 'to + verb'.

 

• Option 4 (in): 'in' – 'insist in' is incorrect.

 

• Other verbs + 'on': rely on, depend on, comment on, congratulate on, dwell on, concentrate on, insist on.

 

• Alternative structure: insist that + clause (They insisted that he pay in advance).

 

NOTE

 

• After a preposition, a verb takes the gerund form (-ing): insisted on paying.

question:
Choose the most suitable preposition from the given options to fill in the blank in the following sentence:

She takes great pride _____ her work.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. in.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The noun 'pride' is followed by 'in' in the expression 'take pride in' (गर्व करना).

 

• Correct sentence: She takes great pride in her work.

 

• 'Take pride in' = to be proud of something one does or owns.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (for): 'for' – 'pride for' is not used in this expression.

 

• Option 2 (on): 'on' – 'pride on' is incorrect; note the reflexive verb 'pride oneself on' (She prides herself on her work).

 

• Option 4 (at): 'at' – 'pride at' is incorrect.

 

• Compare: take pride in (noun phrase) vs pride oneself on (verb) vs be proud of (adjective).

 

• Similar collocations: take interest in, take part in, take delight in.

 

NOTE

 

• SSC frequently tests the trio 'take pride in / pride oneself on / proud of'.

question:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.

He said that his sister had left the house an hour before.
option_1: He said, "My sister had left the house an hour after."
option_2: He said, "My sister left the house an hour later."
option_3: He said, "My sister has left the house one hour before."
option_4: He said, "My sister left the house an hour ago."
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. He said, "My sister left the house an hour ago."

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the indirect sentence, 'had left … an hour before' is the backshifted form of the direct Simple Past 'left … an hour ago'.

 

• While converting indirect → direct: Past Perfect → Simple Past; 'before' → 'ago'; 'his sister' → 'My sister'.

 

• Direct: He said, "My sister left the house an hour ago."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: 'had left … an hour after' – keeps the past perfect and wrongly changes 'before' to 'after'.

 

• Option 2: 'an hour later' – changes the meaning; 'later' refers to a future point.

 

• Option 3: 'has left … one hour before' – present perfect cannot be used with a past time adverb, and 'before' should become 'ago'.

 

• Indirect → direct time words: before → ago; the previous day → yesterday; the next day → tomorrow; then → now; that day → today.

 

• 'Ago' is used with the Simple Past, never with the Present Perfect.

 

NOTE

 

• When converting back to direct speech, reverse every backshift and every time/place change.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice.

He said to me, "Where did you go?"
option_1: He asked me where I had gone.
option_2: He asked me where I went.
option_3: He asked me where I did go.
option_4: He asked me where had I gone.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. He asked me where I had gone.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The direct speech is a wh-question in the Simple Past ('Where did you go?'). The reporting verb 'said to' becomes 'asked'.

 

• The question is changed into assertive order (subject + verb), the auxiliary 'did' is dropped, and Simple Past → Past Perfect 'had gone'.

 

• Pronoun: 'you' → 'I' (the listener is 'me').

 

• Indirect: He asked me where I had gone.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (He asked me where I went): 'where I went' – no backshift of the Simple Past; not accepted under the standard rule.

 

• Option 3 (He asked me where I did go): 'where I did go' – retains the question auxiliary 'did', which is dropped in indirect speech.

 

• Option 4 (He asked me where had I gone): 'where had I gone' – keeps interrogative word order (verb before subject).

 

• Indirect questions always follow statement word order: He asked me where I lived (✗ where did I live).

 

• The question states 'indirect voice'; the correct term is 'indirect speech/narration'.

 

NOTE

 

• Remove 'do/does/did' used for question formation when converting to indirect speech.

question:
Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence with the correct spelling of the word:

The company’s core values are _________ and do not change over time.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. immutable.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct spelling is immutable (अपरिवर्तनीय) — unchanging over time or unable to be changed.

 

• Formation: im- (not) + mutable (changeable, from Latin 'mutare' = to change) → im-mu-ta-ble.

 

• The sentence says the values 'do not change over time', which matches 'immutable'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (immuatable): 'immuatable' – an extra 'a' after 'u'.

 

• Option 3 (imutable): 'imutable' – the prefix 'im-' joined to 'mutable' gives double 'm'.

 

• Option 4 (immutible): 'immutible' – the suffix is '-able', not '-ible'.

 

• Related words: mutation, mutate, mutable, commute, transmute — all from 'mutare'.

 

• Synonyms: unchangeable, fixed, permanent, constant, invariable. Antonyms: mutable, changeable, variable.

 

NOTE

 

• When 'in-/im-' is added to a word beginning with 'm', the 'm' doubles: immortal, immature, immeasurable, immobile.

question: Which of the following words is spelled incorrectly?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Mischievious.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The incorrectly spelt word is 'Mischievious'. The correct spelling is Mischievous (शरारती) – causing trouble in a playful way.

 

• It has only three syllables: mis-chie-vous; there is no 'i' before '-ous'.

 

• A very common spelling (and pronunciation) error is adding an extra 'i' → 'mischievious'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

• Option 1 (Embellishment): 'Embellishment' (decoration/adding details) is correctly spelt.

 

• Option 2 (Discrepancy): 'Discrepancy' (a difference or inconsistency) is correctly spelt.

 

• Option 4 (Catastrophe): 'Catastrophe' (a sudden great disaster) is correctly spelt.

question: Which word is spelled incorrectly?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Disenfranchize.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The incorrectly spelt word is 'Disenfranchize'. The standard spelling is Disenfranchise (मताधिकार से वंचित करना) — to deprive someone of a right, especially the right to vote.

 

• Unlike many '-ize/-ise' verbs, words built on 'franchise' keep the '-ise' ending (franchise → enfranchise → disenfranchise) in both British and American English.

 

• Hence, 'Disenfranchize' is the misspelt option.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (Surreptitious): 'Surreptitious' (done secretly, stealthily) is correctly spelt – note double 'r' and '-titious'.

 

• Option 3 (Magniloquent): 'Magniloquent' (using high-flown, pompous language) is a correctly spelt word – from Latin magnus (great) + loqui (to speak).

 

• Option 4 (Connoisseur): 'Connoisseur' (an expert judge in matters of taste, e.g., art or food) is correctly spelt – double 'n', double 's'.

 

• Words that always end in '-ise' (never '-ize'): advise, advertise, compromise, despise, exercise, franchise, revise, supervise, surprise, televise.

 

• Related 'loqu' words: eloquent, grandiloquent, soliloquy, loquacious.

 

NOTE

 

• Connoisseur is frequently misspelt as 'connoiseur' or 'conoisseur' in SSC options.

question:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:

Has she left the apartment?
option_1: Is the apartment left by her?
option_2: Had the apartment been left by her?
option_3: Has the apartment been left by her?
option_4: Have the apartment been left by her?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Has the apartment been left by her?

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The given sentence is an interrogative in the Present Perfect Tense: Has + subject + V3 + object?

 

• Passive of Present Perfect interrogative = Has/Have + object + been + V3 + by + agent?

 

• The object 'the apartment' is singular → 'Has'. Pronoun 'she' → 'her'.

 

• Passive: Has the apartment been left by her?

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (Is the apartment left by her?): 'Is the apartment left by her?' – Simple Present passive; tense changed.

 

• Option 2 (Had the apartment been left by her?): 'Had the apartment been left' – Past Perfect; tense changed.

 

• Option 4 (Have the apartment been left by her?): 'Have the apartment been left' – subject–verb agreement error; singular 'apartment' needs 'has'.

 

• Interrogative passive keeps the question form: Did he write the letter? → Was the letter written by him?

 

• Pronoun changes in passive: I → me, we → us, he → him, she → her, they → them.

 

NOTE

 

• In interrogative passive, the helping verb agrees with the NEW subject (the former object).

question:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:

The teacher gave the students a difficult assignment.
option_1: A difficult assignment were given the students by the teacher.
option_2: The students were given a difficult assignment by the teacher.
option_3: The students were giving a difficult assignment by the teacher.
option_4: A difficult assignment was given to the students by the teacher.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The students were given a difficult assignment by the teacher.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The verb 'gave' has two objects: indirect object (the students) and direct object (a difficult assignment). Either can become the subject in the passive.

 

• Taking the indirect object as subject (preferred): The students were given a difficult assignment by the teacher.

 

• Simple Past passive → was/were + V3; 'students' is plural → 'were given'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: 'A difficult assignment were given' – subject–verb agreement error (singular 'assignment' needs 'was') and 'to' is missing before 'the students'.

 

• Option 3: 'The students were giving' – Past Continuous active; the meaning is reversed.

 

• Option 4: This is also a grammatically acceptable passive (direct object as subject). However, SSC and most grammar books prefer the personal/indirect object as subject for verbs like 'give', and Option 2 is the listed standard answer.

 

• Two passive forms of double-object verbs: (i) Person + was/were given + thing (preferred), (ii) Thing + was given + to + person.

 

• Double-object verbs: give, teach, tell, show, offer, lend, send, promise, award, pay.

 

NOTE

 

• When two passive forms are possible, choose the one with the PERSON (indirect object) as subject unless the options rule it out.

question:
Read the cloze passage and answer the following questions:

The life of a writer is often romanticized as a journey _______(3) inspiration, creativity, and quiet reflection. While moments of artistic brilliance do exist, the reality is far more (1) arduous than it appears. Writers spend countless hours drafting, revising, and battling self-doubt. The blank page can be both an open canvas and an intimidating void, demanding discipline as much as imagination.

 

A writer’s routine ______(4) greatly. Some work in the early hours of the morning, when the world is still, while others find their rhythm late at night. Many rely on rituals such as a specific desk, a cup of tea, or a walk in the park to spark their creativity. However, inspiration alone is rarely enough; persistence is the real driving force behind completed works.

 

The profession also comes with emotional highs and lows. The joy of finishing a manuscript or receiving praise from readers is often tempered by the sting of rejection letters or critical reviews. Still, writers persevere, fuelled by the belief that _____(5) words can inform, entertain, or even change lives.

 

For many, writing is not merely a career but (2) a calling a lifelong pursuit that shapes the way they see and interact with the world. It is a path that demands patience, resilience, and an unwavering commitment to the craft.

 

In the passage, what does “arduous” most nearly mean?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Difficult and requiring great effort.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Arduous (adjective) means involving or requiring great effort; difficult and tiring (कठिन / श्रमसाध्य).

 

• In the passage: 'the reality is far more arduous than it appears. Writers spend countless hours drafting, revising, and battling self-doubt' – this describes hard, effortful work.

 

• Hence, 'Difficult and requiring great effort' is the correct meaning.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (Easy and quick): 'Easy and quick' – the opposite meaning.

 

• Option 3 (Boring and repetitive): 'Boring and repetitive' – 'arduous' refers to difficulty, not boredom.

 

• Option 4 (Short and simple): 'Short and simple' – contradicts the context of countless hours of work.

 

• Synonyms: strenuous, laborious, gruelling, onerous, taxing, demanding. Antonyms: easy, effortless, simple, light.

 

• Example: an arduous journey through the mountains.

 

NOTE

 

• In context-based vocabulary questions, always verify the meaning with the sentences around the word.

• 'Full of' (adjective) = 'filled with' (participle).

 

NOTE

 

• Cloze tip: read the whole sentence; the words after the blank ('inspiration, creativity…') are contents, which require 'with'.

question:
Read the cloze passage and answer the following questions:

Journalism is often called the fourth pillar of democracy, alongside the legislature, executive, and judiciary. Its primary role is to inform the public, (1) scrutinize those in power, and ensure that citizens can make informed decisions. A free and responsible press serves as a watchdog, exposing corruption, amplifying marginalized voices, and holding institutions accountable.

 

However, this role is neither simple nor without challenges. Journalists frequently operate under intense pressure, balancing the need for (2) objectivity with the realities of deadlines, editorial bias, and, in some cases, censorship. In countries with restricted press freedom, the pursuit of truth can even put reporters’ lives at risk.

 

The rise of digital media has transformed ______(3), making information more accessible but also creating new problems like misinformation and “fake news.” In such an environment, the credibility of journalists depends heavily on rigorous fact-checking and ethical reporting standards.

 

A vibrant and independent press_____(4) essential to the health of any democracy. Without it, power can go unchecked, public debate may wither, and citizens risk being left in the dark. Journalism is not merely a profession; it is a civic responsibility that _____(5) the very foundation of democratic life.

 

The word “scrutinize” in the passage is closest in meaning to:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Examine closely.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Scrutinize (verb) means to examine or inspect closely and thoroughly (बारीकी से जाँच करना).

 

• The passage says the role of journalism is to 'inform the public, scrutinize those in power' – i.e., to watch and examine the actions of the powerful carefully, as a watchdog.

 

• Hence, 'Examine closely' is the closest meaning.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (Ignore): 'Ignore' – the opposite of scrutinize.

question: What is the antonym of "Resilient"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Weak.

question: What is the antonym of "Vigilant"?

question:

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

• Option 3 (Wise): 'Wise' – the opposite; wise customers would not be deceived.

 

• Option 4 (Guilty): 'Guilty' – the antonym of 'innocent' in its legal sense.

• The line is from R.K. Narayan's short story 'An Astrologer's Day'.

• In context-based synonym questions, choose the meaning that fits the sentence, not just the dictionary's first meaning.

question:
Which of the following pairs of homonyms can be used to fill in the blanks most suitably?

Her slow _____ through the company ranks came only after earning the _____ of every senior executive.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. ascent, assent.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ascent (noun) = a rise to a higher position or rank; climbing up (चढ़ाई / उन्नति). 'Her slow ascent through the company ranks'.

 

• Assent (noun) = approval or agreement (सहमति / स्वीकृति). 'after earning the assent of every senior executive'.

 

• Hence the correct pair is ascent, assent.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (ascent, ascent): 'ascent, ascent' – the second blank needs 'approval' (assent), not 'rise'.

 

• Option 2 (assent, assent): 'assent, assent' – the first blank needs 'rise' (ascent), not 'approval'.

 

• Option 4 (assent, ascent): 'assent, ascent' – the two words are placed in reverse order.

 

• Other pairs: accent (way of speaking) – ascent – assent; descent (going down) – dissent (disagreement) – decent (proper).

 

• Presidential assent: a Bill becomes an Act after the President's assent (Article 111 of the Constitution).

 

NOTE

 

• 'Ascent' and 'assent' are homophones — same pronunciation, different spelling and meaning.

question:

• Prefix 'extra-' also appears in: extracurricular, extraterrestrial, extrajudicial.

• In synonym questions, the three wrong options here all mean 'ordinary', making the answer clear.

question:

The niece had an exquisite sense of drama in her storytelling.

question:

solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. palate, palette.
